notes.title: In time together
notes.science: Moving in time with someone can make you trust them more. In one study, people who sang or walked in step cooperated more afterward.
notes.limits: A tapped beat is a tiny stand-in for a song.
notes.counter: Some say closeness comes first and the rhythm follows.
notes.question: Does a greeting need words at all?

sources.label: Synchrony and Cooperation, Wiltermuth and Heath, 2009

notes.title: Taking turns
notes.science: In ten languages from around the world, people waited about the same short gap, near a fifth of a second, before taking their turn in talk.
notes.limits: The game counts beats, not feelings.
notes.counter: Turn taking can also be a ritual with no warmth in it.
notes.question: When does a habit become a bond?

sources.label: Universals and Cultural Variation in Turn-Taking in Conversation, Stivers and others, 2009
